title: Anthropic IPO could create thousands of multimillionaire employees
summary: The average Anthropic employee could be worth over $40 million after the company's IPO today, according to SEC filings and investors.
body: The average Anthropic employee could be worth over $40 million after the company's IPO today, with over 400 employees likely to be worth over $100 million, according to SEC filings and investors. At a share price of $83, Anthropic's market value would top $1.4 trillion, making it one of the 10 most valuable companies in the U.S. It will not only be the largest IPO in history by dollar amounts, but it is also shaping up to be one of the most rapid wealth creation events in history. Follow CNBC' s live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut Anthropic was founded just five years ago and has only 5,300 employees. According to SEC filings, the artificial intelligence company has generated 1.77 billion options for employees, with a strike price of $2.91 a share. It has also paid out over 1 billion restricted stock units. If the stock trades at $83 a share, the combined wealth of Anthropic employees will be around $232 billion, based on their share count in the filings. The total works out to an average of $44 million per employee. Yet because many of the employees are later hires, earlier employees could have supersized gains since they've accumulated more stock. According to investors in the company, at least 400 early employees will be worth $100 million or more at a $83 share price. Several could become billionaires, they said. The employee total doesn't include the seven founders, who each own between 230 million and 240 million shares, which will each be worth around $20 billion based on a $83 share price. While employees face complex lockup periods and vesting schedules, the wealth is likely to start making its way into the economy quickly, economists say. The first two areas will be the San Francisco real estate market and philanthropy. Brokers say San Francisco's already red hot real-estate market will get a boost from hundreds of Anthropic employees who now have more liquid stock they can borrow against. An analysis by Redfin found that Anthropic's current and former employees will have enough post-IPO wealth to buy 9% of all the homes in San Francisco. Anthropic's culture of effective altruism, along with its generous matching program for charitable gifts of employee shares, are expected to spark a wave of giving, especially to donor-advised funds. Employees hired before May 17, 2024 can pledge up to 50% of their vested shares for a 3-to-1 match by the company. Later hires can pledge up to 25% for a 1-to-1 match. The seven co-founders have also pledged 80% of their wealth to charity. "Philanthropy could be the piece that's different this time," said Michael Faust, president of wealth management at Bailard Inc. "Some of the companies going public now really encourage their employees to give, and they match it. That could make a huge difference for Bay Area nonprofits for a long time to come."

title: Data center electricity use could double by 2030, IEA says
summary: Global electricity use by data centers could double by 2030 as the AI boom adds pressure to power grids across the world, according to the IEA.
body: Global electricity use by data centers could double by 2030 and stretch power grids, potentially delaying new projects, the International Energy Agency warned. Data centers could consume around 1,000 terawatt-hours of electricity a year by 2030, according to the IEA, which added that tight supply chains, local opposition and limited grid capacity could slow construction. The warning is part of the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario , in which the agency forecasts are based on measures that have been put forward but have not yet been adopted. The IEA cites large data center project pipelines in Texas, Virginia, Finland and the U.K. In several regions, the combined capacity of data centers waiting to connect exceeds current peak demand. Without grid upgrades, power networks could become more congested and less reliable, the IEA said. New projects could face longer waits to connect, while generators could be forced to cut output when the grid cannot meet demand. Peak electricity demand is projected to rise 40% to 50% by 2035, according to the IEA. Under the Stated Policies Scenario, grids should be expanded by 26 million kilometers of new lines by 2035, while about 16 million kilometers of existing lines need to be replaced or refurbished. Supplies of copper, cables and transformers are already tight, the IEA said. Under the Current Policies Scenario, which is based on energy policies and regulations already in place, grid spending is projected to rise 75% over the next decade. The agency says power networks are "one of the biggest energy investment stories of the next decade." The scenario projects that renewable power generation will grow 85% more in the next decade than in the previous one. Solar photovoltaics would become the world's largest source of electricity from the late 2030s Electricity would account for nearly 30% of global final energy consumption by 2035, up from 23% in the IEA's main scenarios. The IEA said the 2026 energy crisis could accelerate electrification as countries seek to reduce their reliance on imported oil and gas. Electrification can reduce exposure to imported fuels, but it also makes a reliable power grid more important. Before the Iran war, an average of 20 million barrels of crude oil and oil products a day transited the Strait of Hormuz in 2025 — about 25% of global seaborne oil trade. The strait also carried nearly 20% of global LNG trade. "The pressures of the current crisis must not obscure the choices that will shape energy security, sustainability and prosperity for the decades to come," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said.

title: Traders Seek Long-Term Crude Supply Deals with Qatar
summary: The biggest international oil trading houses are in talks with state-owned QatarEnergy to receive supply of Qatari crude oil for 2027 amid recovering flows through the Strait of Hormuz and traders’ experience of shuttling crude through the chokepoint in wartime conditions. While some refiners are still hesitant to commit supply from the Persian…
body: What I Cover Tsvetana Paraskova is an energy and commodities journalist who has contributed to Oilprice.com for nearly a decade, covering global energy markets, commodities,… The biggest international oil trading houses are in talks with state-owned QatarEnergy to receive supply of Qatari crude oil for 2027 amid recovering flows through the Strait of Hormuz and traders’ experience of shuttling crude through the chokepoint in wartime conditions. Some of the largest commodity traders are asking for Qatari crude for 2027, mostly the Qatar Marine and Land grades, anonymous sources involved in the talks earlier this month have told Bloomberg . While some refiners are still hesitant to commit supply from the Persian Gulf for next year, the trading houses, which have braved the Strait of Hormuz risks and shuttled a lot of crude through it in recent months, are more willing to strike year-long deals for next year. The deal-making for the oil trading giants has been made easier by recovering flows through Hormuz, falling Middle Eastern crude prices amid expectations of glut, and weaker competition from refiners. QatarEnergy’s talks with refiners have been slowed amid importers’ concerns about shipping and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil trading giants are less wary as they have taken on a leading role in moving crude out of the Persian Gulf since the Iran war began. Crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have rebounded since August to almost pre-war levels. Despite the highest number of attacks on tankers in October, flows have held so far as producers and traders have continued to adapt to shuttle-shipping cargoes through Hormuz and then onto separate vessels via ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman. In addition, smaller oil tankers moved in October the most volumes of crude oil out of the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, as Iran targets supertankers and incidents with naval mines and unknown projectiles hit a wartime high. Gulf producers and oil importers have had to continuously adapt to the changing security and shipping conditions in and around the Strait of Hormuz. With supertanker rates soaring to record highs in September and early October, and attacks on very large crude carriers (VLCCs) jumping to a wartime high, sellers, traders, shippers, and buyers have started to lean more on the smaller-sized vessels to move crude out of the Persian Gulf. body: What I Cover Tsvetana Paraskova is an energy and commodities journalist who has contributed to Oilprice.com for nearly a decade, covering global energy markets, commodities,… India imported a record-high level of crude oil volumes in October, trade data showed on Thursday, as volumes from Saudi Arabia jumped to an eight-month high amid a recovery in Gulf shipments. India imported a record 5.58 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil last month, up by 4.7% compared to September and a 6.9% rise from October 2025, according to the trade data cited by Reuters . Russia remained the single largest oil supplier to India, with Indian imports rising by 3.5% in October compared to September. At 1.85 million bpd, India’s crude oil imports from Russia accounted for about one-third of total purchases. Russia remains a key crude oil supplier to India, but the rebound in Hormuz flows and the shorter distance to India have boosted Indian imports of crude oil from the Gulf producers. Saudi Arabia significantly raised its shipments to India, to an eight-month high of 790,000 bpd in October, according to the trade data. The Kingdom thus toppled the United Arab Emirates (UAE) from the second spot of India’s top oil suppliers. Indian oil imports from the UAE slumped to 612,000 bpd in October, a seven-month low. So Russia remained the biggest oil supplier to India in October, followed by Saudi Arabia, which overtook the UAE for the first time since the war began. The Saudis, apart from boosting exports, offered discounts for their crude grades to offset higher shipping costs, beating the other Middle Eastern producers on pricing, refining sources in India told Reuters. At the end of October, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), one of the biggest Indian state-owned refiners, said it would reduce its purchases of crude oil from Russia in November as high freight costs and premiums for Russia’s crude undermine the attractiveness of Moscow’s oil compared to multiple offers for Middle Eastern crude, whose prices are falling. title: The Middle East War Has Wiped 2.8 Billion Barrels Off Global Oil Supply
summary: The war in the Middle East has caused global oil supply losses of a total of 2.8 billion barrels plus 60 billion cubic meters of natural gas, the International Energy Agency estimated in its latest World Energy Outlook, released today. Under the IEA’s current policies scenario, both oil and gas demand will continue growing, with the driver of that…
body: What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… The war in the Middle East has caused global oil supply losses of a total of 2.8 billion barrels plus 60 billion cubic meters of natural gas, the International Energy Agency estimated in its latest World Energy Outlook , released today. This disruption is going to affect oil demand, the IEA predicted, but only if governments around the world stay the course with accelerated electrification to reduce consumption of hydrocarbons. Under the IEA’s current policies scenario, both oil and gas demand will continue growing, with the driver of that demand shifting from road transport to petrochemicals. Under the stated policies scenario, which is based on ambitions rather than firm commitments, oil demand is seen “levelling off” at around 103 million barrels daily before beginning to decline gradually. Natural gas demand in this scenario continues rising until the mid-2030s and then plateaus. The IEA added another scenario to its modelling in this year’s edition of the World Energy Outlook, called the Additional Response Case, in which oil and gas supply disruption extends in time, prompting extra efforts to secure energy supply. Under that scenario, the IEA believes oil demand could start declining sooner, shedding 4 million extra barrels daily by 2035 compared to the state policies scenario. “The Hormuz crisis has delivered a huge shock to the system. While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be. And I don’t see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before,” the IEA’s head, Fatih Birol, said . The IEA noted that the Hormuz disruption has prompted a search for alternative routes, which could result in significantly reduced flows through the chokepoint in the future, from 20 million barrels daily before the war to just 8.5 million barrels daily in 2030 and less than 2 million barrels daily in 2035. body: What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… The European Parliament and EU member states agreed today to delay the so-called methane regulation by two years under pressure from the top oil and gas supplier, the United States, and the continued disruption of normal supply resulting from the war in the Middle East. The European Parliament cited as a reason for the delay the supply disruption caused by the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran: “Importers have warned they may not be able to secure enough compliant supplies at a time when energy markets are strained and prices high due to the conflict in the Middle East,” the EP said in a statement. It added that the regulation will come into effect in 2029, when suppliers and buyers both would need to start reporting on the “methane intensity of the fossil fuels they place on the EU market.” The methane regulation was a problem for the United States long before it started bombing Iran at the end of February. In fact, both the U.S. and Qatar repeatedly warned against the methane regulation, saying it would disrupt the EU’s oil and gas imports, because it is literally impossible to track every hydrocarbon molecule and its methane content, as U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright noted more than once. “There is no viable path to compliance with the regulation”, Wright and his Qatari counterpart Saad al-Kaabi wrote in a joint letter this June. “Because legal compliance remains paramount, exporters and importers alike are unwilling to enter into contractual agreements that knowingly violate EU law.” The methane regulation was formally adopted by the European Union two years ago, aimed at reducing not only the bloc's own emissions of the greenhouse gas that constitutes almost 100% of natural gas but also forcing countries outside the EU that do business with the bloc to cut their emissions as well, notably gas suppliers. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $92.01 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $83.00 per barrel, as forecasters warn of a glut even though tanker tracking data shows flows out of the Persian Gulf are still below pre-war levels, despite the significant improvement from the early months of the war. body: What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… Crude oil prices steadied today after a decline earlier this week, as the perception of a return to oversupply and continued attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz basically canceled each other out. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $92.01 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $83.00 per barrel, as forecasters warn of a glut even though tanker tracking data shows flows out of the Persian Gulf are still below pre-war levels, despite the significant improvement from the early months of the war. Meanwhile, risks remain high. Vortexa this week said that Iran had designated more than 50% of the tankers Gulf petrostates are using to transfer their oil to the Gulf of Oman and from there to global markets. “So far the restrictions have not reduced the volume of oil moving through the shuttle relay,” the analytics firm said, adding that exporters are adapting by adding another stage of ship-to-ship transfers. This is helping keep a steady flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf, but risks remain, as Iran issues daily reports of tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz as they try to move outside the channel that Tehran has designated for free movement. Still, “Further disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz remain an important upside risk, but rising OPEC+ output, resilient Russian exports and building US inventories point to a more comfortable supply picture,” Ing commodity strategists said in a note on Wednesday. Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey added they expected the oil market to gradually rebalance, curbing oil prices’ potential for moving consistently higher. Additional pressure on prices came from the U.S. Fed, which has signaled it may raise rates, which would weigh on oil demand growth, further limiting the scope for a further increase, Reuters noted in a report earlier today. The Fed meets next in December to decide on rate policy. body: West Texas Intermediate faces an interesting issue after Fridayâs inventory report. It really isnât just a question of global supply increasing or demand weakening. Instead, traders need to consider whether American crude can compete in international markets at current price differentials. The Energy Information Administration reported on November 18 that commercial crude inventories increased by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels during the week ending November 13. Reuters reported that analysts had expected an increase of just 58,000 barrels. This difference does make quite a bit of difference, in so much as we need to process what this could mean going forward. The market was already concerned about global supply, but a substantially larger American inventory build adds another problem for WTI. The international pricing relationship helps explain why WTI has been particularly vulnerable. When American crude is sufficiently inexpensive compared with Brent, exporters can profitably ship barrels to overseas customers. Freight charges, crude quality, and other costs can determine these transactions and whether or not they make commercial sense for the end user. However, Reuters cited Sparta Commodities analyst Jun Goh on November 18 as saying that WTI export arbitrage to Asia and northwestern Europe had effectively closed. In practical terms, American oil wasnât inexpensive enough relative to international alternatives to justify the shipping cost. This can leave additional crude in the domestic market for Americans. A widening Brent-WTI differential may eventually correct the problem by making exports more competitive. But meanwhile, domestic petroleum product inventories have also increased. Distillate stocks rose 1.6 million barrels to 104.9 million barrels. Gasoline inventories increased 5.2 million barrels to 215.9 million barrels. This combination should be paid attention to because a crude inventory build accompanied by rising product inventories can suggest that petroleum supply is temporarily exceeding demand across several parts of the refining system. Nevertheless, weekly inventories can fluctuate quite wildly, and the next report will be especially important in determining whether this represents some type of deterioration thatâs going to have any legs to it. title: 2026 Delivers 'Double Major Surprise' to Oil Markets - Rigzone
body: In a commodities research report sent to Rigzone by the Goldman Sachs team this week, analysts at the company, including Daan Struyven, noted that 2026 has delivered a “double major surprise” to oil markets. “First, the effective closure of Hormuz - previously seen as an unlikely tail scenario - did not only materialize but also lasted much longer than expected at the start of the war, leading the market to upgrade 2026 oil price expectations,” the analysts highlighted in the report. “Second, given the actual length of the shipping disruptions, oil prices have risen less sharply than expected,” they added. The “key reason” for this, according to the analysts, is that global inventory declines from March to October were limited to around 600 million barrels, or around five percent of global estimated stocks at 2.4 million barrels per day. The analysts outlined in the report that this was because of the 2025 pre-war surplus worth around 300 million barrels of builds from March to October and “remarkable oil market adaptation”. Outlining this adaptation, the analysts flagged the recovery in Persian Gulf oil output “despite ongoing shipping risks given pipeline redirections, dark exports, U.S. Navy escorts, and ship-to-ship transfers (which contained the March-October 2026 loss in Gulf oil output vs. its 2025 average to ~2050 million barrels); the decline in oil demand in response to higher prices, “especially in Q2 and in China, which switched to power and coal (reducing net global stock draws by ~775 million barrels); and the strength in oil output outside the Gulf, “especially Brazil (reducing draws by ~375 million barrels)”. Looking at 2027 in the report, the Goldman Sachs analysts stated that they again expect a contest between high supply disruption risk and continued market adaptation. “In our view, the range of plausible geopolitical outcomes in 2027, especially for the U.S.-Iran war, remains exceptionally wide for two reasons,” they noted. “First, achieving a sustainable U.S.-Iran diplomatic breakthrough is likely to remain challenging, especially agreeing on the governance of the Strait of Hormuz and on the sequencing of any mutual concessions,” they added. “Second, the longer the standoff lasts without a deal, the more the odds of Iranian escalation might rise,” they continued. The analysts outlined in the report that, under their base case assumption of neither a definitive sustained diplomatic breakthrough nor a re-escalation with major long-term damage to oil infrastructure, “staying nimble and leaning against excessive swings in the risk premium is likely to remain a successful strategy for trading oil markets in 2027”. “While oil prices gradually ease in 2027 on further adaptation in our base case, the crude risk premium now appears quite low relative to the still significant geopolitical risks,” the analysts said. “We estimate that the risk premium in Brent spot prices has dropped from $27 on the Friday before the midterms to only a few dollars last week as market sentiment swung sharply with the U.S.-Iran conflict not immediately escalating post midterms,” they added. title: Oil settles lower as WTI falls 3.2% to $83.26, its lowest since August, after US crude and gasoline stocks rise more than expected - MLQ.ai
body: Oil prices fell on Wednesday, Nov. 18, after US crude and fuel inventories rose more than analysts expected. US benchmark West Texas Intermediate settled down $2.75, or 3.2%, at $83.26 a barrel, its lowest since Aug. 26, and global benchmark Brent settled down $1.19, or 1.28%, at $91.95, Reuters reported [1] . Losses were steeper earlier in the session: at 1:16 p.m. ET, WTI was down 4.44% at $82.19 and Brent was down 2.18% at $91.11 [1] . The Energy Information Administration's weekly report showed crude inventories up 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million in the week ended Nov. 13, compared with the 58,000-barrel rise analysts expected in a Reuters poll [1] . Gasoline stocks rose 5.2 million barrels against a forecast 1.6 million, and distillates rose 1.6 million barrels against a forecast 1.3 million [1] . Analysts at Gelber & Associates said attacks on commercial shipping still threaten deliveries through the Strait of Hormuz, "but those risks have provided limited support against the growing expectation of a global surplus" [1] . The gap between the two benchmarks was at its widest in about two weeks on Tuesday, LSEG data showed, and WTI fell more steeply on Wednesday [1] . "WTI arbitrage trades have been shut to Asia and Northwest Europe, thus WTI correcting more than Brent is the expected price movement to allow the arbitrage window to open again," said June Goh of Sparta Commodities, who added that rising US Gulf Coast crude stocks were also widening the spread [1] . The US-Iran conflict limited the decline [1] . Iran said it attacked US drone and missile sites in Kuwait overnight after a US strike on Qeshm Island, and ADNOC L&S said one crew member was missing and 11 were injured after one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday [1] . Energy shares followed crude lower. The S&P 500 energy sector was down nearly 3% at midday, the worst performer in the index, with Exxon Mobil and Chevron each down more than 3% and ConocoPhillips and EOG Resources down more than 2%, CNBC reported [2] . title: Nvidia Stock Slides After Earnings: Extra Week Makes $130B Guidance 4% Growth, Not 12% - Tech Times
body: Nvidia's $130 billion fourth-quarter revenue guidance implies about 4% growth in weekly revenue over the quarter it just reported, not the 12% headline gain, because the new quarter runs 14 weeks and the old one ran 13. The Santa Clara, California, chipmaker reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion on Tuesday, Nov. 17, in its first earnings report under interim CEO Colette Kress, and its shares closed Wednesday, Nov. 18, down 2.89% at $150.96 . That calendar effect matters to anyone who owns Nvidia directly or through an index fund, and to any company budgeting for AI servers, because it changes how fast demand is actually growing. The same report showed supply commitments rising to $390 billion from $279 billion in one quarter, mainly for multi-year memory purchases. Nvidia guided fourth-quarter revenue to $130 billion , plus or minus 3%, and its release says the quarter includes "an additional week." Kress confirmed the extra week on the earnings call, where she tied it to operating-expense guidance of about $11 billion on a GAAP basis, a figure that also reflects transition-related costs. Third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion was up 20% from $96.2 billion in the prior quarter and up 103% from a year earlier. On a raw basis, $130 billion is 12% above $115.8 billion. Spread evenly, though, $115.8 billion over 13 weeks is about $8.9 billion a week, while $130 billion over 14 weeks is about $9.3 billion a week, a gain of roughly 4%. Lee Yang's Investing.com analysis reaches the same conclusion, saying growth works out "closer to 4% rather than 12%" if sales are spread evenly. The plus-or-minus 3% range brackets that figure. The low end, about $126.1 billion, is roughly 1% weekly growth, and the high end, about $133.9 billion, is roughly 7%. Sales may not arrive evenly across a quarter: Nvidia's CFO commentary tied higher receivables to shipment linearity from its Rubin launch and extended payment terms. The guidance still beat the roughly $125 billion analysts expected , and third-quarter revenue topped a consensus near $109 billion . Nvidia's GAAP gross margin was 74.8% in the third quarter, and the company guided the fourth quarter to between 71.0% and 72.0%. At the midpoint, that is about 3.3 percentage points, or roughly $4.3 billion less gross profit on $130 billion of sales than the third-quarter margin would have produced. Kress said on the call that she expects a bottom in fourth-quarter margins , with margins recovering to 72% to 73% in fiscal 2028, and she raised the fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to about 75% from 70%. The trough is not new. TechTimes projected in August a fourth-quarter margin low of 71% to 72% and a recovery to 72% to 73% in fiscal 2028. The CFO commentary does not explain the larger fourth-quarter decline, but it does tie the small third-quarter dip to the initial Rubin ramp and says inventory rose to "support our Rubin product ramp." Rubin brought in nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, Kress said on the call. That is roughly 18% to 19% of the $107.6 billion Data Center total, in line with the roughly 20% share that preview coverage had flagged. Each Vera Rubin NVL72 rack packs 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs into one liquid-cooled unit. Memory is also why the commitments jumped, and it comes with its own supply math. High Bandwidth Memory stacks up to 32 DRAM dies joined by through-silicon vias, and the newest HBM4 standard uses a 2048-bit interface that allows up to 2 terabytes per second per stack. Wikipedia's account of the market says memory prices have risen in compounded increases since early 2025, some exceeding 200%, because every HBM ramp consumes wafer capacity that general-purpose memory would otherwise use. For buyers, the consequence is that accelerator supply and ordinary DRAM prices draw on the same wafers. title: Nvidia beats Q3 estimates with $115.8 billion revenue, yet shares slip - Startup Fortune
body: A record-sized quarter was supposed to settle the argument about Nvidia. Two days on, the stock is telling you the argument was never only about demand. Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion on Tuesday, November 17, up 103% from a year earlier and well ahead of the roughly $109.1 billion analysts had expected, according to LSEG consensus figures cited by IBTimes. Non-GAAP earnings came to $2.68 a share, above the $2.50 or so the Street was looking for. Data center sales did the heavy lifting at $107.6 billion, up 110% on the year, per Nvidia's own release. The outlook was bigger still. Nvidia guided fourth-quarter revenue to $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, against the $125.25 billion LSEG consensus. Then it added the line that matters most for anyone modelling the stock: the guidance assumes no data center compute revenue from China at all. The first reaction looked like the beat deserved. Shares rose nearly 4% in extended trading, IBTimes reported. By Wednesday that was gone. A market report on the day had Nvidia down another 2.89%, which is a strange thing to do after a quarter that doubled sales and a forecast that clears consensus by about four percent. Look at what the stock had already been through. On November 12, Jensen Huang resigned as CEO after more than three decades at the company he co-founded. The board named Colette Kress, Nvidia's CFO since 2013, as interim CEO while it keeps the CFO job, and says it's searching for a permanent successor. Shares fell as much as 14% on the open that Thursday, their lowest since June 2025, and IBTimes noted the stock walked into the report down about 17% for the year. Nvidia's $108 billion fiscal third-quarter forecast assumes it sells zero AI data center chips to China, even though analysts peg potential Chinese demand at $30 billion. Trump hosts Xi Jinping in Washington on September 24, with Jensen Huang expected at the state dinner and chip access on the agenda. - Nvidia China AI chip sales forecast outlook - state dinner Xi Jinping impact on Nvidia revenue So Tuesday's results were also Kress's first earnings report in the top job. Her line in the release was upbeat: "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater." The numbers back her up. Nvidia said Vera Rubin NVL72, its newest rack-scale system, had the fastest product ramp in the company's history, with shipments already going to major cloud providers. It also lifted its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75%, according to one market summary of the call. Frankly, that's the point. Nobody on the buy side was in doubt that the chips are selling. What they can't price is who runs the company next, what the board does about it, and whether a CFO holding two jobs is a bridge or a long-term answer. A beat can't answer a question that isn't about the beat. Even the cleanest detail in the release carries a small warning. Gross margin was 74.8% on a GAAP basis this quarter, and Nvidia guided to 71.0% to 72.0% for the next one. Revenue is climbing faster than the margin on each dollar of it. Nvidia has now told investors twice in plain words that it isn't counting on China. Reuters, as relayed by IBTimes, reports the exclusion reflects US export limits on advanced AI processors, and it applies to data center compute rather than every product sold there. That makes $130 billion a number with no Chinese upside baked in. It also means any licence that does come through is a bonus, not a rescue. The company is also spending its way through the noise. Nvidia returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter through buybacks and dividends, and has $227.3 billion left on its repurchase authorization after the board added $150 billion in September. A quarterly dividend of $0.25 a share is due December 23. Per Reuters via IBTimes, the board is not considering bringing Huang back. body: Trillion-dollar spending on data centers and chips is reshaping US dollar dynamics, but the outlook splits forecasters The US dollar has a new co-pilot, and it runs on GPUs. Artificial intelligence is increasingly steering the greenback’s fortunes, or at least the massive investment race built around it is. That debate was laid out in a November 19 Reuters column by Mike Dolan out of London. It comes as the dollar sits at its strongest level in 19 months, a run that some analysts tie directly to AI spending. Investment in AI data centers, chips and computing equipment has ballooned into a trillion-dollar phenomenon. Analysts at Barclays and Deutsche Bank have been connecting the dots. In their view, the surge in AI capital expenditure is fueling stronger GDP growth, firmer inflation and higher interest-rate expectations. The scale is hard to ignore. AI-related activity has been linked to at least one-third of US GDP growth in 2026. The most direct channel to the dollar runs through foreign buyers. When overseas investors want a piece of US AI stocks, they first need dollars to buy them. Analysts predict more than $1 trillion in foreign equity inflows could support the dollar in 2026. Deutsche Bank analysts have put a name on one piece of this loop. They identified what they call a “chipdollars” cycle, linking Asian chip surpluses to purchases of US equities. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. The dollar index was up approximately 3.1% year-to-date as of November 2026, and it recently notched its strongest position in 19 months. Barclays and Deutsche Bank have adjusted their forecasts accordingly. Both expect dollar strength to persist into the first half of 2027, with sustained AI capex acting as a tailwind. The analysts suggest the Federal Reserve could potentially shift toward a more hawkish stance as conditions evolve, which would typically add further support to the currency. The analysts flag several risks. A slowdown or downgrade in AI capital spending sits at the top of the list, followed by volatility in equity markets. The third risk is subtler. Traditional safe-haven flows into the dollar may decline, which would change the currency’s character in ways that matter during a crisis. Historically, the dollar has often benefited when markets panic, as investors rush toward the perceived safety of US assets. An AI-driven dollar works differently: its strength depends on optimism about growth and stocks. For investors, the clearest implication is that the dollar and AI stocks are becoming more intertwined. Moves in one may increasingly echo in the other. It also raises the stakes around AI-related headlines. Earnings from chipmakers, guidance on data center budgets and any sign of spending fatigue could now ripple into currency markets, not just tech indexes. Countries on the other side of the chipdollars loop have a stake as well. Asian chip exporters benefit from the buildout, and their surpluses feeding back into US stocks means they are, in effect, co-investors in the AI dollar trade. Barclays and Deutsche Bank are betting the tailwind lasts into early 2027. Disclosure: This article was edited by Diego Almada Lopez. body: Nvidia spent $58.1 billion buying other companies’ stock in the nine months ending Oct. 25—nearly 12 times the $4.95 billion it spent in the same period last year, according to the quarterly results it posted late Tuesday. This almost matches the $61.2 billion Nvidia spent on stock buybacks, up from $36.3 billion last year. It was Nvidia’s first earnings report without Jensen Huang as the CEO. The company reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the three months ending Oct. 25, more than double the $57 billion the year prior and beating analysts’ expectations of $109 billion . The near-even split between outside stakes and buybacks shows Nvidia’s growing dual role as both chip supplier and investor in the AI industry, with its equity investments “focused on frontier labs, infrastructure financiers, and other private companies,” according to its Q3 2026 CFO commentary (Nvidia has invested in OpenAI and Anthropic ). This raises the question of circular financing—whether Nvidia is funding the demand that drives its chip sales. And if AI spending falters, Nvidia could suffer from both lower chip sales and falling valuations for the companies it has invested in, said James Kisner, the managing director of technology at equity research firm Water Tower Research. “It’s magnified and you feel more pain because you’re kind of double exposed here,” Kisner told Fortune . Kisner said that Nvidia’s billions in free cash flow means it can afford to pour $58.1 billion into other companies’ stock, but that can be seen as fueling its own demand. Equity securities only generated $1.8 billion in net gains –which included a $1 billion loss from non-marketable equity securities—for Nvidia in Q3. “If you were really cynical, you could say, ‘Oh, like these guys are just generating their own demand,’’’ Kisner said. Still, Kisner said Nvidia has incentives to keep investing given how much its growth has benefitted shareholders. It became the first company to cross the $5 trillion market valuation mark last year , though it has since dropped to $3.7 trillion as of Nov. 18, per Yahoo Finance data . “There are all kinds of incentives for them to fuel the fire if they have the cash, so there’s a self-serving aspect,” he said. “The markets really reward them for pouring all this money.” He said the strategy reflects Huang’s approach of “spreading money around and kind of keeping the ecosystem going,” and he sees interim CEO Colette Kress continuing it with “a little more conservatism” at the margins. Kress told analysts on the Nov. 17 earnings call that giving returns to shareholders is a “super top priority,” with Nvidia having $227.3 billion left under its stock buyback authorization program that Kress said it intends to use “by the end of fiscal 2028.” But she said another priority is supporting Nvidia’s suppliers who “are working feverishly to build more” and might need “assistance in terms of capital.” “We want to make sure that we’re there for them so they can move as quickly as possible,” Kress said . “I think that is a very great use of our capital to help support that part of it.” Nvidia is also willing to help finance select customers’ data centers, but Kress told analysts it’s “a lot of work to understand if those are the right types of investments” for Nvidia to make. “It is a process that we will look very deeply in terms of the company, the strength of what they have planned, as well as everything that they need in terms of that data center to do so,” Kress said. But Nvidia’s financial backing of the AI industry doesn’t stop at that. Kress said on the call that Nvidia’s future commitments to neoclouds, the small firms that buy Nvidia chips and then rent out computing capacity, totaled $32 billion in Q3. Separately, she said Nvidia’s total credit guarantees reached $118 billion, including $105 billion in credit support for the PORTS-Pike data center project in Ohio, which will host NVIDIA infrastructure under a 20-year lease with OpenAI . title: Is Summit Insights Wrong to Give Up on NVIDIA? Wall Street Still Sees $251 - TIKR.com
body: NVIDIA ( NVDA ) reported $115.8 billion of third-quarter revenue on Nov. 17, up 103% from a year ago, and raised its revenue growth outlook for next year to about 75% from 70%. A day later, Summit Insights Group analyst Kinngai Chan downgraded the stock to Hold from Buy, with no price target. At the Nov. 18 close of $150.96, NVIDIA sat 37% below its Oct. 6 closing high of $239.24. NVIDIA said on Nov. 12 that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO, four days after the board opened an independent investigation into his conduct. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and the board isn’t considering Huang’s return . Chan pointed at exactly that, saying the leadership change makes NVIDIA’s roadmap beyond Vera Rubin less certain and warning that the Commerce Department’s Nov. 16 rule could hurt NVIDIA and the wider AI industry in 2027. The rule requires licenses to ship advanced AI chips to overseas data centers that supply significant computing power to companies headquartered in China or other restricted countries. China’s commerce ministry threatened countermeasures the next day. NVIDIA’s outlook already assumes no data center compute revenue from China. Gross margin is falling too, from 74.8% on a GAAP basis in the third quarter to a guided 71% to 72% in the fourth, which Kress expects to be the bottom. The average analyst price target is now $251, 66% above the Nov. 18 close and down from $329 in late October: On Nov. 18, Jefferies and Wells Fargo cut their targets to $250 from $300 and kept their Buy and Overweight ratings. Earnings estimates are moving the other way. Consensus EPS for the year ending January 2028 is up 23% over the past 90 days, and the $16.24 analysts now expect is more than triple fiscal 2026’s $4.77: Yet the stock trades at about 10x forward earnings, its lowest in five years and under a third of its 36x five-year average: The $251 average target is 11.7x the $21.44 analysts expect per share for the year ending January 2029. The Street isn’t asking for a return to 36x, only for the estimates to hold and a modest lift from 10x. See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on NVIDIA, along with Wall Street’s revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See NVIDIA’s Analyst Ratings NVIDIA’s guarantees could still break the bull case. Its maximum exposure under them reached $118 billion at the end of the third quarter, including $105 billion of credit support for an Ohio data center campus leased to OpenAI. Summit has a point, but cutting a stock at about 10x forward earnings, with estimates still rising, looks late to me. Most of the bad news is already in the price. The CEO pick and the fourth-quarter report will show whether I’m right. Revenue near the $130.0 billion guide (helped by an extra week), with gross margin inside 71% to 72%, would say the business runs fine without Huang. title: Anthropic IPO, AI wealth spawn a new, leaner kind of family office
summary: The Anthropic IPO and a flood of AI wealth are spurring the creation of new family offices built for the era of artificial intelligence.
body: The Anthropic IPO is expected to mint hundreds of centimillionaires and spur the creation of new investment vehicles to manage these windfalls. Anthropic-related wealth could lead to 15 to 20 new single-family offices over the next three years, according to exclusive data provided to CNBC by Altss, a global private markets intelligence platform. Altss also estimates about 70 households related to the Anthropic wealth boom will start working with multifamily offices or outsourced family offices. Altss' CEO Dawid Siekiera added that the firm expects the launch of a flurry of other personal investment companies, venture funds and investor partnerships. Lawyers and family-office consultants told CNBC that they have received inquiries from current and former Anthropic employees and early investors about potentially setting up their own firms. Many of these newly wealthy tech professionals are interested in leaner operations with few in-house staff and leveraging technology and outside consultants to manage their fortunes, they said. "Why would they be building a traditional office when they can probably see inherently by where they built their wealth how to make it more efficient?" consultant Kirby Rosplock told CNBC. "I think there's a sense that they can do it smarter, and that may not mean having more headcount, but more horsepower." Anthropic beneficiaries, like their peers in tech, tend to skew younger, with some even in their late 20s, experts told CNBC. They are typically more focused on hands-on investing than preserving generational wealth compared to traditional family office principals, according to Rosplock. (A Deloitte survey estimated the average age of family office principals at 68.) "This is very different than having a multi-generational family business that is acquired by some other larger firm," she said. "These people are likely staying engaged in the space, wanting to take the next bite at the apple and continue to build wealth." While these Silicon Valley clients often have better access to hot startups than traditional investment advisors, they typically aren't familiar with a broad range of asset classes, according to Chris Mays of Armanino, an accounting and consulting firm. "When you look at the financial services folks, a lot of times they would build the investment function inside of their family offices. I don't see that as a likely outcome inside of these [tech] family offices," he said. "They're going to rely on third-party investment advisors or multi-family offices. They're not going to go and hire a buy side guy out of x, y, z hedge fund or private equity fund to run their money." Jennifer Katrulya, CPA and partner at PKF O'Connor Davies, said she recommends relying on outside advisors rather than building out an in-house investment team. "You're going to get the deeper expertise from the wider bench. The minute you try to hire someone for that expertise, unless you're investing in their growth, they're becoming stale every day after you hire them," said Katrulya, co-leader of the accounting and advisory firm's family office group. For young, first-time wealth creators, a founder's office may be more appropriate than a traditional family office, according to partner William Kambas of the law firm Withers. Founder's offices often have similar legal infrastructure as family offices but are typically smaller, with fewer levels of management and a focus on assisting the principal with personal needs and investments. "A lot of young entrepreneurs have ideas and they want the flexibility to execute on their vision," Kambas said. "A family office or a management office simply gets in the way because they're going to do it all themselves." Michael Kosnitzky, a partner at Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman, said that the costs of a traditional family office aren't necessarily worth it to most Anthropic beneficiaries. body: The raw materials index was led by a 65.6% increase in crude oil, which tells most of the story and that continued in October but the negative reading was driving by lower prices for gold, silver, and platinum group metal ores Statistics Canada tracks producer prices through two monthly releases: the Industrial Product Price Index (IPPI) and the Raw Materials Price Index (RMPI). Both are typically published together at 8:30 am ET a few weeks after the reference month ends, and together they serve as Canada’s version of a producer price index for goods. The IPPI measures prices Canadian manufacturers receive for products as they leave the plant, across a wide range of industries including refined petroleum, lumber and wood products, primary metals, chemicals, food and beverages and motor vehicles. The RMPI measures what manufacturers pay for their key inputs, such as crude oil, metal ores and concentrates, logs, grains, livestock and crude vegetable products. Many of those raw materials are imported or priced off global benchmarks, so the RMPI largely tracks world commodity markets. Neither index is seasonally adjusted, and both are reported as monthly and annual changes. Because energy carries such a large weight, StatCan also publishes the IPPI excluding energy and petroleum products and the RMPI excluding crude energy products, which give a better sense of broader cost pressures. The exchange rate plays an outsized role. Many Canadian goods are priced in US dollars, so when the loonie weakens, the Canadian-dollar value of those products rises and lifts the IPPI even if underlying prices haven’t changed. A stronger loonie has the opposite effect. The reports cover goods only and don’t feed into a central bank target measure, so they rarely move the Canadian dollar or rate expectations. They’re watched mainly as an early signal of cost pressures that could eventually reach consumer prices and as a window on how commodity swings, currency moves and tariffs are affecting Canadian producers. Of those, 79% expect competitors to raise prices, and the median expected timing shortened to three months from four. Those price hikes are going into softer demand: 42% of firms say customers have become more price sensitive since last quarter. The forward capex index is the other line to watch. title: Hormuz Oil Exports Could Decline amid Inbound Tanker Shortage
summary: Analysts are touting the remarkable recovery in crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf, which have jumped close to pre-war levels in recent months. body: What I Cover Tsvetana Paraskova is an energy and commodities journalist who has contributed to Oilprice.com for nearly a decade, covering global energy markets, commodities,… Analysts are touting the remarkable recovery in crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf, which have jumped close to pre-war levels in recent months. The oil market reflects the bearish sentiment, with Brent Crude prices sliding in the past weeks to around $92 per barrel, down from a recent peak of over $118 per barrel in late October. The market and most analysts assume that the steady flow of crude oil from the Strait of Hormuz and the entire Middle Eastern region will continue into the next months, rebalancing supply and demand and even tipping the balance into a large surplus next year. However, in the volatile situation in and around the Strait of Hormuz, with no recent rapprochement for potential U.S.-Iran talks, nothing is given, and no forecast has more than 50/50 odds of panning out. The Iran war has reshuffled trade routes and patterns and tied up more tankers in inefficient and lengthy voyages. The increased flows of oil from the Strait of Hormuz, mostly thanks to ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in the Gulf of Oman, are tying up supertankers for weeks waiting for the transfers outside the Strait, limiting the availability of very large crude carriers (VLCCs) for the other global key oil trade routes, such as the U.S. Gulf Coast to Asia. The inefficient shuttle shipping is tying up a growing number of smaller vessels, Suezmaxes and Aframaxes, too, on the Hormuz trade. This leaves fewer available empty tankers globally willing to travel to the Middle East to pick up cargoes in the Gulf of Oman. The total capacity of the empty tankers going to the Middle East has slumped by some 40% since the end of August, per data from Tankertrackers.com cited by Bloomberg . There are “not enough vacant tankers to take oil out of the region,” Tankertrackers.com’s co-founder, Samir Madani, told the publication. “It’s one thing to bring the oil out into the Gulf of Oman via the Strait of Hormuz, but it seems like there isn’t enough to take the oil out of the Gulf of Oman,” the analyst said. As of November 16, the combined capacity of ballasting supertankers and Suezmaxes en route to the Gulf of Oman has slumped to 71 million barrels, down from 130 million barrels capacity at the end of August, according to data compiled by Tankertrackers.com. To be sure, flows from the Middle East remain elevated, albeit somewhat lower so far in November compared to October. Crude oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz have held so far despite the worst month for attacks on tankers in the area since the war began. The high crude oil export levels despite increased security risks give the market and many analysts confidence that the only path forward is continuous recovery and, ultimately, an oil glut within months. Tanker rates have dropped from the record highs seen in early October, but they remain above historical norms and pre-war levels amid heightened war insurance premiums and security risks. “Security risks continue to weigh on tanker operations in the Gulf,” Maria Bertzeletou, Senior Market Analyst at Signal Group, wrote in an analysis this week. “Repeated attacks continue to restrict the pool of owners willing to accept Gulf employment, while elevated war-risk insurance costs and operational delays add to voyage expenses and limit effective vessel availability.” So far this month, Iran has been reporting nearly daily incidents of tankers hitting naval mines in corridors that Iran has designated as “unauthorized” in the Strait of Hormuz. Non-Iranian observers and organizations also report more frequent attacks on tankers in and near the Strait of Hormuz. Anyone hoping that cash lands in power stocks should look at the calendar first. The prospectus puts Anthropic's computing and infrastructure commitments at about $895 billion, but Inc. counted only about $70 billion of that due before September 2027. Most of what Anthropic needs from the energy industry was ordered, leased or reserved before the book closed, so the useful question is who already holds a signed contract. Entergy supplies the power for Hut 8's Louisiana site. GE Vernova has no disclosed Anthropic contract at all. It's here because Anthropic's prospectus, as Fortune reported , warns that the company may pay above-market prices for equipment with long lead times, and GE Vernova's order book shows what a long lead time looks like. body: Natalia Katona is a freelance commodity analyst, based in the United Arab Emirates. This year Brazil is set to add more oil than any other producer in the world. And this offshore production boom came at the right time for a global oil market that has been short of barrels reaching refiners without passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Brazilian crude output hit a record 4.7 million b/d in September , up 20.3% year-on-year. Historically, a major part of Brazil’s first exports went to Asia. It’s no surprise that the first price assessments for Brazilian grades came about in China, a country that dominated the early years of Brazilian exports. However, Brazil’s incremental supply is forcing the state-owned company Petrobras and other producers to diversify their pool of buyers, looking beyond Asia. After the ban on Russian crude imports in 2022, Brazil has started making inroads into Europe, with this year seeing unprecedented levels of crude flows to the Old Continent. Brazil will need buyers both in Asia and Europe as more offshore capacity comes online. Since October 2024, state-controlled Petrobras has brought six major projects into production, including new units at the giant Buzios and Mero fields . Together with Equinor’s Bacalhau , those projects account for roughly 1.3 million b/d of capacity, some of which is still ramping up. Petrobras is expecting two more Búzios platforms, P-80 and P-82 , to start producing in 2027. Hence, for Brazilian producers, the question is where they can sell those additional barrels at the best return after freight and taxes. Until this year, freight accounted for much of the difference between selling to Europe and selling to Asia. That changed in March, when the Brazilian government introduced a 12% crude export tax after the US-Iran war sent oil prices into triple-digit territory. Calculated on the FOB value of the cargo, the new tax allowed the Brazilian administration to capture part of the windfall and, in turn, subsidize the prices of diesel as the Latin American giant remains dependent on imports from abroad. The government has since extended it three times, most recently through December 31 . Brazil’s export tax eventually turned out to be Europe’s advantage. The EU secured preferential terms under its interim trade agreement with Mercosur this year. Signed in January and provisionally applied from May 1 , the agreement requires Brazil to reduce qualifying export duties by at least 50% for EU-bound shipments. At a FOB price of around $77/bbl, a Brazilian producer pays $4.62/bbl in tax on a sale to the EU against $9.24/bbl on a sale to China or India. That leaves room to offer a European refiner a price marginally below market levels and still earn more on the barrel. By August, EU-bound loadings had reached 975,000 b/d, almost double pre-crisis February’s 490,000 b/d. The EU’s share of Brazilian exports rose from 22% to roughly 34% over the same period. Brazil ranked fifth among the EU’s crude suppliers, behind the US, Norway, Kazakhstan and Libya. Discounts on Tupi and Búzios have made both grades cheaper for European refiners than Norway’s Johan Sverdrup even after freight. Brazilian cargoes have gone to the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp region, Spain, Portugal, Poland, France and Italy. Even Norway took in some Brazilian crude, although shipments there do not qualify for the EU tax rate. Whilst historically Brazil’s crude exports were mostly revolving around Tupi and Buzios, the recent boost in second-generation giants such as Mero has provided European refiners with additional flexibility to choose their most convenient grade. Mero flows have almost tripled between 2024 and now to 570,000 b/d and the 29° API grade is increasingly becoming Europe’s favorite. Its sulphur content is the lowest amongst Brazil’s top three grades (0.31%), making it the most convenient option for coastal refiners seeking to produce IMO 2020-compliant VLSFO. Under existing rules, EU countries must maintain…
body: Julianne Geiger is a veteran energy journalist and market analyst with more than a decade of experience covering the global oil and gas sector. Her… The European Union wants countries to stockpile the fuels they actually use, following a nine-month Middle East conflict that has exposed a problem with Europe's emergency oil reserves: having enough oil in storage doesn't necessarily mean having enough diesel or jet fuel. The European Commission is preparing changes that would require member states to align their emergency reserves more closely with national fuel consumption and refining capacity, according to a draft seen by Bloomberg on Thursday. Under existing rules, EU countries must maintain emergency oil stocks equivalent to at least 90 days of net imports or 61 days of domestic consumption, whichever is higher. The rules already require a portion of those reserves to consist of refined products, but they don't require countries to stockpile those products in proportions that reflect domestic demand. That distinction has become increasingly important as Europe's refining capacity is on the decline. The bloc produces more gasoline than it needs. However, it remains structurally short of diesel and especially jet fuel, according to the European Commission's autumn economic forecast. Crude oil reserves cannot immediately replace missing diesel or jet fuel imports. According to Eurostat, EU emergency reserves totaled 103.5 million metric tons in July, including 43.7 million tons of crude oil and 36.5 million tons of gasoil and diesel. Thirteen member states held stocks below their minimum requirements that month. The financial consequences of Europe's fuel import dependence have been substantial. Between March and September, the Iran war added an estimated €40 billion ($44 billion) to the bloc's diesel import bill. Jet fuel imports cost an additional €16 billion to €19 billion, according to EU estimates. Europe is already drawing on emergency reserves. The International Energy Agency said last week that its members would release another 71 million barrels through February, including approximately 15 million barrels of diesel, largely from France and Germany. The Commission's proposal would also permit temporary military access to emergency fuel reserves under exceptional circumstances. The draft could still change before the Commission's planned approval in early December. body: Haley Zaremba is an energy journalist and researcher with more than a decade of professional experience covering global energy systems, land and natural resources, and… We finally have hard data to show us exactly how much energy data centers are using in the United States, and the results are staggering. Driven by the artificial intelligence boom, energy-hungry data centers are popping up in record numbers around the country and driving up domestic energy demand after decades of plateaued growth. Data center hyperscalers in the United States alone now rival the energy demand of entire other nations, with worrying implications for energy security, economic inflation, and the climate. But AI development is careening full speed ahead, and energy companies are only too eager to cash in. A new study , published in the highly respected scientific journal Nature Sustainability this week, found that the growth of hyperscale data centers (HDCs) has significantly increased energy demand and carbon emissions in the United States. Just 403 of these large-scale data centers designed for massive scalability to support runaway AI growth accounted for nearly two percent of the country’s total electricity consumption between May of 2024 and April of 2025 – and those numbers doubtless have only grown in the intervening year and a half. This is a landmark study, providing the first peer-reviewed figures for data center emissions since the start of the AI boom. The sector has operated under an extreme degree of opacity as policymakers, oversight bodies, and researchers alike have struggled to keep up with the ultra-powerful, secretive, and rapidly evolving sector. The study also found that the majority of the energy used to power those data centers came from fossil fuels. Indeed, while Big Tech is providing considerable funding for research and development for cutting-edge and next-gen clean energy technologies like nuclear fusion and space-based solar power , it is also causing a major natural gas boom across the United States. As a result, Big Tech’s emissions are ballooning out of control. According to company figures, the carbon emissions of Google and Microsoft each skyrocketed by 25 percent year-over-year from 2025 to 2026, while Amazon's increased by 16 percent . Altogether, over the course of the last fiscal year, these three companies emitted 19 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, equaling about a third of the output of the nation of France. And, worryingly, “only a handful of small countries” have yet to sign on to a COP31 pledge to “power and build AI infrastructure and hardware sustainably” as part of the United Nations’ climate conference wrapping up this week in Antalya, Türkiye. What’s more, the runaway energy consumption of data centers is driving up prices for consumers as inflation hits hard across the United States . This has put hyperscalers in the crosshairs of politicians on both sides of the aisle . And last month’s blue wave election is expected to bring harsher levels of scrutiny and policy oversight to the sector. “Between Democrats’ sweep of Congress and Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia, the AI bubble has rarely looked so close to bursting,” Tim McDonnell, climate and energy editor for nonpartisan news outlet Semafor, recently wrote in an opinion piece for the outlet. body: What I Cover My focus spans the global energy landscape and the technologies reshaping it, specifically focusing on oil and gas, renewables, and tech-driven market… Venezuela is using artificial intelligence to reduce emissions and increase efficiency in its oil and gas industry, a senior official told Reuters on the sidelines of the COP31 summit in Antalya, as the world’s biggest crude reserves holder looks to boost production. Venezuela will not stop pumping oil, Albania del Mar Villarroel Gomez, vice minister for AI and efficiency in hydrocarbons, told Reuters. “Our policy is not to stop producing hydrocarbons,” the official told Reuters, as Venezuela defends its right to keep pumping oil to help its economic recovery. “Our goal is to reduce waste and emissions while maintaining energy production,” added Villarroel, whose office was created earlier this year by acting President Delcy Rodriguez at the Ministry of Popular Power for Hydrocarbons, which oversees the oil, gas, and petrochemical sectors. Venezuela is currently using AI to monitor emissions from oil and gas production and detect methane leaks, as well as to improve operations at oilfields, Villarroel told Reuters. Venezuela, the only major oil and gas producer in Central and South America that hasn’t signed the Global Methane Pledge, accounted for about half of all fossil fuel emissions in Central and South America in 2025, according to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) Global Methane Tracker 2026 . Moreover, the upstream methane emissions intensity of oil and gas operations in Venezuela is nearly six times the global average, and flaring intensity is around 12 times higher, the IEA has found. Venezuela, which plans to boost oil production in a controversial deal with the Trump Administration, will use smaller specialized AI models to track emissions and optimize oilfield production, instead of relying on hyperscaler systems, Villarroel told Reuters. In June, SLB signed a long-term framework agreement with Venezuela’s state oil firm PDVSA to support the revitalization and modernization of Venezuela’s oil and gas sector. A key focus of the agreement is the digital transformation of Venezuela’s oil and gas sector. SLB and PDVSA plan to assess how connected data, predictive models, and AI-enabled workflows can help improve efficiency, accelerate decision-making, and strengthen the industry’s operating foundation, the oilfield services giant said. title: Tudor dumps copper miners, doubles down on gold, silver
summary: He is the second billionaire this week, after Druckenmiller, to offload copper assets as metals face fresh volatility.
body: He is the second billionaire this week, after Druckenmiller, to offload copper assets as metals face fresh volatility. Billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones’ hedge fund, Tudor Investment Corporation, has piled into gold and silver miners while exiting major copper producers, including Teck Resources (TSX: TECK.B) (NYSE: TECK) during the third quarter, a new regulatory filing shows . The hedge fund increased its shares in the world’s largest gold miner, Newmont (NYSE: NEM) (TSX: NGT) by 132.5%, and in silver miner Hecla Mining (NYSE: HL) by 159.8%, according to the Form 13F it filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Nov. 16. Tudor completely exited Teck Resources as well as Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE: SCCO). Tudor held over 2.85 million shares in Teck, which were worth over $169 million on Sept. 30, 2026. It also reduced its stake in Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) by almost 90%. The sales come at a time where metal prices were hitting record highs, before the current market erosion. Tudor’s filing does not establish whether the fund has abandoned its broader bullish outlook on copper. The filing showed where the company was investing up until Sept. 30, 2026. A 13F covers long positions in US-listed equities, ETFs and listed options only, excluding short stock positions, futures (including gold and copper futures), physical metal, swaps, bonds and currencies, and most non-US listings. As copper miners exited the portfolio, gold and silver ETFs took their place. Tudor increased its shares on the Vaneck Gold Miners ETF by 195.7%, and in Ishares Silver Trust by almost 40%, each one worth about $41 million on Sept. 30, 2026. While Tudor cut shares in two other gold ETFs that were worth about $95 million on Sept. 30, 2026, it entered two new silver ETFs worth about $2 million, trying to gain more ground in silver as it has in gold. Among individual producers, Tudor also bought new shares in Eldorado Gold Corp . (TSX: ELD) (NYSE: EGO) and silver miner Endeavour Silver Corp (NYSE: EXK) (TSX: EDR). The fund was more selective elsewhere in the sector, trimming its stake in gold miners Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX, NYSE: AEM) and Barrick Mining (TSX: ABX) (NYSE: B) by over 28% and 37%, respectively, and exited Alamos Gold (TSX: AGI; NYSE: AGI). The mixed transactions suggest Tudor was reallocating capital within precious metals rather than making an across-the-board bet on gold and silver producers. Beyond mining equities, the fund established uranium-related investments valued at approximately $17 million. Gold, copper and silver have all faced lows in the past few weeks driven by interest rate hikes and tensions in AI. Gold hit $3,710.29 per ounce on Thursday, along with silver hitting $45.28 per ounce and copper $12,554 per metric ton, all decreasing in comparison to September 2026. The changes may signal a move towards more security in the long-term, as geopolitical tensions and Fed decisions loom over the markets, than a complete move away from copper. “It reinforces the enormous risks that the economy is facing right now, and it’s those uncertainties and the anxiety that those risks create that cause investors to say ‘I should have more of my money in gold and silver,’” CPM Group managing partner Jeffrey Christian said on an interview with the Northern Miner Podcast . Similar to Druckenmiller, Tudor Jones’ shift raises questions about what precious metals show him that he no longer sees in copper. Investors just need to see if it will pay off. The hedge fund sold its entire holding in aluminum producer Alcoa (NYSE: AA), previously comprising more than 470,000 shares worth $24.5 million, and reduced its position in diversified miner Rio Tinto (ASX, LON: RIO) by 42.1%. Outside the metals sector, Tudor nearly doubled its holding in BlackRock’s Bitcoin exchange-traded fund to $64.6 million.

title: Vizsla delays first silver at Panuco by a year

body: Vizsla now targets first silver at Panuco in the second half of 2028. Developer Vizsla Silver (TSX, NYSE American: VZLA) has pushed back its target for first production at the Panuco project in Mexico by a year as it prepares for a phased return to the site following the abduction and killing of 10 workers in Sinaloa. The stock dropped. Vancouver-based Vizsla now targets first silver in the second half of 2028, according to a statement Thursday. Engineering is about halfway complete and about 85% of the planned processing plant equipment has been ordered. Permitting, site readiness and construction timing figured in the revised schedule. “We stand by the families of our colleagues and share their grief in this profound loss, as well as their need for answers,” CEO Michael Konnert said in the release. Vizsla shares dropped 5.2% to $4.04 Thursday morning in Toronto, just above their 52-week low of $4.03. That values the company at about $1.4 billion (US$999 million). Gunmen abducted the Vizsla workers in the municipality of Concordia on Jan. 23. The remains of the last missing worker were identified in July, Mexican newspaper El Independiente reported. Vizsla has committed US$5 million to a foundation for communities in Sinaloa and plans to contribute a share of future profits. The foundation would supplement the company’s direct assistance to affected families. Mexican federal authorities announced arrests in connection with the case in September. In October, Mexico’s defence ministry reported further arrests and said it had linked those detained to the abductions and killings. Vizsla says it continues to assist the investigation. Silver and gold mining in the Panuco-Copala district dates back centuries. Vizsla began exploring there in 2019 and moved to consolidate ownership of the district in 2021 by exercising two options. Its current mine plan calls for two underground mines, Copala and Napoleon, feeding a single plant. Security concerns had already interrupted work at Panuco. Vizsla paused fieldwork in April 2025 and resumed it the following month. After the January abductions, the company again suspended some work at and near the site while engineering continued remotely. Vizsla says it’s working with Mexican federal authorities and security advisers on a phased return. Panuco still needs key federal approvals. Vizsla submitted its environmental impact assessment in February 2025 and said in its annual filing that Mexico’s environment ministry had asked for more information. A land-use change authorization is also required before construction. Vizsla has yet to make a production decision. Its November 2025 feasibility study put initial capital at $238.7 million and projected payable output of 94.7 million oz. of silver and 776,000 oz. of gold over 9.4 years. The study’s estimates don’t reflect the revised schedule, potential cost increases or financing costs.

title: Friedland’s Ivanhoe Electric strikes high-grade copper in Arizona
summary: Ivanhoe Electric's latest drilling reveals two mineralized zones at Gleeson, raising prospects for a new US mining district.
body: Ivanhoe Electric's latest drilling reveals two mineralized zones at Gleeson, raising prospects for a new US mining district. Robert Friedland in 2014 at the site of the initial Kamoa discovery in DRC. ( Image: Govind Friedland via CEO.ca ) Ivanhoe Electric (NYSE American: IE; TSX: IE), backed by mining billionaire Robert Friedland, has discovered high-grade copper-gold-silver mineralization at its Gleeson project in southeastern Arizona, making it the company’s top exploration priority. The company reporte d Thursday that drilling identified two mineralized zones, including 123.6 metres grading 0.91% copper, 0.44 gram of gold per tonne and 5.27 grams of silver per tonne from a depth of 601.7 metres. The interval included 71.03 metres grading 1.38% copper, 0.52 gram of gold and 6.73 grams of silver. “These initial drill results are some of the best copper-gold-silver intercepts drilled in the Western United States in the last ten years,” executive chairman Friedland and CEO Taylor Melvin said in a joint statement. The discovery, 28 miles north of Arizona’s historic Bisbee mining district, could provide another growth opportunity alongside Ivanhoe Electric’s Santa Cruz Copper Project near Casa Grande, where it plans to produce refined copper domestically. The results come as copper prices plunged about 6% this week to $12,471 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange, their lowest since April. Investors have been unwinding bets on artificial intelligence-driven demand and potential US tariffs on refined copper, with the sell-off accelerating after billionaire investor Stan Druckenmiller turned bearish . The decline contrasts with tight physical supplies in China, where the Yangshan copper import premium reached a record $360 per tonne, up from less than $100 in September. Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories fell 18% over the week to 27,600 tonnes, their lowest since December 2023, highlighting the divide between investor sentiment and physical market conditions. Drilling at Gleeson has outlined an upper copper-gold-silver-bearing breccia zone spanning approximately 500 by 500 metres, beginning around 600 metres below surface. The mineralization thickens southwestward and remains open in several directions. A second hole, CGD26-TR-008, returned 381.66 metres grading 0.34% copper, 0.29 gram of gold and 1.07 grams of silver per tonne from 587.85 metres. It included 16.2 metres grading 1.04% copper and a separate 41.51-metre interval grading 1.23 grams of gold. Deeper drilling, below 1,000 metres, identified intrusive-hosted, skarn and carbonate-replacement mineralization containing copper, gold, silver and zinc. The system extends roughly 800 metres north to south and 600 metres east to west, with further potential to the west. “The initial drill holes at Gleeson are the most impressive I have seen in my 20-year career at an early-stage exploration project,” senior vice-president of exploration Alex Neufeld said. Neufeld compared Gleeson’s geology with the nearby Bisbee district, which produced more than 200 million tonnes of ore over 133 years. Ivanhoe Electric controls approximately 20,000 acres of mineral rights and more than 2,000 acres of private surface rights at Gleeson, although drilling has tested only a small portion of the property. Since November 2025, the company has completed 11 drill holes, receiving full assays for seven and partial results for two. Two rigs are operating, with 16,000 metres of drilling targeted by year-end. Additional holes have encountered visible sulphide mineralization, including deeper carbonate-replacement zones beginning around 1,250 metres below surface. Gleeson remains an early-stage discovery without a defined mineral resource or demonstrated economic viability. Further drilling must establish the continuity, scale and true widths of the mineralized zones.
