body: Gold fell to its lowest level in 14 months on November 18, trading near $3,770 per ounce. The metal briefly plunged to $3,660 before partially recovering. Now, investors want to know whether the correction has run its course, and what 2027 could bring. Gold is a precious metal that investors often treat as a safe haven. However, it pays no interest, so it becomes less attractive when yields rise. That dynamic explains much of the current slide. Gold hit its lowest level since September 2025 amid a firm dollar and rising rate expectations. It now trades roughly 32% below its early-2026 peak near $5,600. As a result, the metal is on track for its weakest annual performance since 2015. US Treasury yields have climbed above 5%, which raises the cost of holding non-yielding assets. Moreover, traders see another Federal Reserve rate hike in December as nearly certain. As Bloomberg noted, persistent inflation pressure keeps that outlook in place. The selloff also reflects profit-taking after gold's record run earlier this year. Meanwhile, central banks and some ETFs have kept buying. Still, elevated real yields and the broader rates environment continue to dominate short-term price action. Many banks think so, although they have trimmed their near-term targets. Goldman Sachs recently cut its end-2026 forecast to $4,150. The bank also lowered its end-2027 projection to roughly $4,650 to $4,800. Even so, it expects central banks to keep buying about 60 tonnes per month. According to Goldman, gold could gain more strongly once the Fed pivots to rate cuts later in 2027. Lower rates would reduce the opportunity cost of holding the metal. In addition, a weaker dollar could revive demand from overseas buyers. Other institutions see even higher prices. UBS targets $5,000 to $5,400 by mid-to-late 2027. Bank of America projects an average of $4,800 to $5,000 next year, while CIBC sees about $5,200. Both banks cite structural demand and possible renewed de-dollarization concerns. Separately, a Reuters poll puts the median 2027 forecast at $4,650. "We expect prices to consolidate and recover in the coming months," said Standard Chartered's Suki Cooper, cited by Reuters. For now, volatility remains high. The quick rebound from $3,660 shows that buyers still step in at lower levels. Whether that support holds could decide gold's next move. The Wall Street Journal reported that front-month November COMEX gold settled at $3,736.80 an ounce yesterday, down 3.16% , while December gold finished around $3,740. The daily explanation is not that difficult to understand. As the expected path of interest rates rises, the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset like gold rises with it. Dollar strength can add a second obstacle for buyers measuring gold in other currencies. This is consistent with the selloff, but it should not be expanded into a mechanical rule that yields always determine the gold price. Gold is a liquid reserve asset and can be sold to raise cash when investors need it to reduce exposure across markets. Those figures are somewhat elevated, but they do not show a further daily rise in those yields on Wednesday. This is precisely why a current gold decline should not automatically be described as a result of a same-day rise in every Treasury yield. The broader expected rate path, nominal yields, the dollar, and liquidation pressure can all matter separately. body: A gold price of $5,250 per ounce in the fourth quarter of 2027 is Morgan Stanley’s forecast, approximately 35% above the spot price used in its report. With gold falling to its lowest in more than a year, the projection ranks among Wall Street’s more bullish calls. In its 2027 Global Strategy Outlook, issued on 15 November, Morgan Stanley put gold first among its commodity picks. Its projected price path takes the metal to $5,000 per ounce in the second quarter of 2027, then to $5,250 by year-end. Market consensus is significantly lower. Goldman Sachs, whose latest outlook appeared on Monday, forecasts an end-2027 price of $4,650 per ounce, leaving its target $600 below Morgan Stanley’s. Monday’s brief drop in spot gold to $3,830.74 per ounce underlined the metal’s recent weakness. That marked its lowest price since early October 2025, down 31.5% from January’s record high of $5,594.82 this year. Even so, Morgan Stanley sees a degree of resilience in gold despite the unfavourable macroeconomic environment. In the bank’s view, this indicates that conventional interest rate models no longer provide a complete explanation for price movements. Inflationary pressures generated by the Middle East conflict have prompted a return to interest rate rises by the Federal Reserve this year. A stronger US dollar has accompanied persistently high long-term bond yields worldwide. Gold would normally face headwinds in these circumstances: with no interest income from the metal, an increase in real interest rates makes holding it more costly in terms of forgone returns. Applying the relationship observed between gold and US 10-year real yields from March to July this year to current conditions would put the metal’s theoretical price below $3,000 per ounce. Its actual price, however, remains around $3,900. Central bank buying of physical gold and money flowing into gold ETFs have helped counter, in part, the drag from elevated interest rates and dollar strength. An estimated 675 tonnes of gold were bought by central banks worldwide in the first three quarters of this year, according to the World Gold Council. The official sector thus remains a significant source of demand, even as some of the largest buyers have adjusted the pace at which they build their holdings. Market Insight: Rates and Dollar Strength Could Keep Gold Under Pressure A 96.6% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate rise in December, against 3.4% for a 50-basis-point increase, shows that markets still widely anticipate another hike. Morgan Stanley’s 2027 forecasts place the US 10-year Treasury yield at 5% and the US Dollar Index at 105, implying a rise in both. Together, the interest rate and currency backdrop could prolong the near-term pressure on gold. The bank is nevertheless maintaining cautious portfolio positioning despite its ambitious price target for the end of 2027. An increase in its gold allocation depends on signs that expectations for Federal Reserve policy and market interest rates are settling. The important question is not which one of those observations will be correct; itâs whether the shortage being forecast is large enough, sufficiently immediate, and located in the right part of the physical market to offset selling driven by interest rates and investment positioning. The Silver Instituteâs November 12 interim update projects a 35 million-ounce global silver deficit in 2026, making what would be a sixth consecutive year of demand exceeding supply. Its projection for total demand is 1.08 billion ounces, down 5% year over year. Against that, the Institute expects industrial demand of 640 million ounces, down 3% for the year. These are metal-focused estimates reported by the Indice Association and, as yet, are not audited year-end outcomes. The detail inside industrial demand is more revealing than the aggregate. The Institute expects industrial applications outside photovoltaics to grow 4.5% this year, even as silver consumption in solar cells falls under pressure from material thrifting and substitution. In practical terms, photovoltaic manufacturers have an incentive to use fewer milligrams of silver per cell when the input becomes expensive. Industrial growth in electrical and other uses may coexist with declining total industrial silver demand. This distinction also changes the medium-term bull case. Itâs not sufficient to argue that more solar installations must translate into more silver consumption. Output can grow while silver intensity per unit declines. For a credible demand story, analysts need to track both the number of units manufactured and the metal used in each one. body: Higher prices are dragging down silver demand; however, the market will still chart its sixth annual supply deficit. The Silver Institute projects demand will outstrip supply by 35 million ounces. Last year, the silver market charted a 40.2-million-ounce (1,250.36 tonnes) market deficit. Earlier this year, the Silver Institute forecast a slightly higher deficit of 46.3 million ounces. Higher prices have created headwinds for industrial demand, while falling prices have softened investment demand. The projected 2026 supply shortfall will increase the cumulative 6-year deficit to approximately 746 million ounces. To put that into perspective, analysts expect silver miners to produce 834 million ounces this year. Before this string of successive market deficits, there was a cumulative above-ground stock rise of 243 million ounces between 2010 and 2020. Cumulative silver stocks have declined by 473 million ounces over the last 15 years. This metal shortage drove two silver squeezes. The first pushed silver to over $50, and the second took it to well over $100. When silver demand outstrips mining and recycling volumes, users must source silver from existing above-ground stocks. This tends to nudge prices higher, incentivizing holders to release metal into the market. The Silver Institute expects total demand to dip by 5 percent to 1.08 billion ounces this year. Industrial demand is expected to fall about 3 percent in 2026, despite a 4.5 percent increase in non-photovoltaic offtake. Even so, total industrial demand is expected to hit the fourth-highest level on record at 492 million ounces. Higher silver prices have put a significant drag on demand for silver in solar panels as manufacturers accelerate thrifting and substitution. Bar and coin demand is forecast to come in around 215 million ounces, a 2 percent year-on-year decline. However, physical silver investment demand will remain around 13 percent higher than in 2024. U.S. retail investment is expected to reach its lowest level since 2010. Indian demand has also fallen off, partly due to increased import duties imposed last summer. Analysts say Indian demand will likely decline around 10 percent this year. The Silver Institute forecasts that jewelry and silverware demand will decline by 22 percent and 17 percent, respectively, this year. Analysts say higher prices and weaker rural spending in India are incentivizing purchases of smaller, lighter products. Changing consumer preferences in China and subdued demand in Europe and the U.S. have also weighed on jewelry volumes. Interestingly, overall jewelry spending has increased slightly despite the decline in volume. Silver mining output is expected to remain flat, dipping by 0.5 percent. Meanwhile, the higher silver price is encouraging recycling. The Silver Institute projects recycled silver volumes will rise around 6 percent this year. Significant silver outflows from ETFs, combined with softer demand, have eased the physical market tightness that drove two silver squeezes last year. However, the Silver Institute says ETF silver holdings have recovered by 24 million ounces since the end of June, partially reversing first-half outflows.

title: Copper’s Recent Selloff Could Present Long-Term Buying Opportunity, UBS Says: Report - TradingView
body: UBS reportedly believes copper’s recent sell-off could present a long-term buying opportunity, but cautioned investors against rushing in, as further price declines remain possible. Analyst Daniel Major said the weakness appears to reflect a positioning reset rather than a fundamental deterioration in copper demand, according to an Investing.com report on Thursday. At the time of writing, Southern Copper Corp (SCCO) shares were down 2.2%, Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) declined more than 3%, while Teck Resources (TECK) fell 2%. The analyst said copper prices have come under pressure amid concerns over AI spending, uncertainty following the U.S. midterm elections, and stronger-than-expected inflation data that raised expectations of further rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. Major said that while AI contributes relatively little to copper demand directly, a sharp slowdown in spending by major tech companies could hurt the broader economy and weaken demand for the metal. Last week, Goldman Sachs also reportedly warned that its $15,400-per-ton forecast for 2027 faces downside risks from AI-related investor positioning and weaker U.S. tariff expectations. On Wednesday, three-month copper futures closed at $12,471 per metric ton on the London Metal Exchange (LME), their lowest close in seven months. Copper futures for December deliveries were trading 0.6% lower at $5.66 per pound at the time of writing. UBS identified near-term technical support at $12,000 per ton on the LME and $5.50 per pound on COMEX. The analyst expects copper mine supply to grow by only about 1% in 2027. Major also warned that more than 950,000 tons of excess U.S. copper inventory could return to the global market if expectations of American import tariffs weaken. Despite copper prices falling, retail sentiment surrounding the United States Copper Index Fund (CPER) on Stocktwits turned ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours. The fund has declined around 3% so far this year. Meanwhile, FCX has fallen 3% over the same period, underperforming both TECK and SCCO.

title: Oil prices rise as tanker disruptions offset surplus supply outlook - CNBC
body: Oil ​prices inched higher on Thursday as investors focused ​on fresh reports of tanker disruptions in the ​Strait of Hormuz, helping the market recover from the previous session's selloff driven by rising US inventories and surplus forecasts. Brent crude futures rose 77 cents, or 0.8%, to $92.72 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for December delivery gained $1.08, or 1.3%, to $84.34. The December contract expires on Friday, while ⁠the ‌more actively traded January contract advanced 91 cents, or 1.1%, to $83.21, with trading volumes ⁠nearly seven times those of the front-month contract. Two oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday and "exploded," Iran's navy said in a statement carried by state media. Reuters could not independently verify the report. The Iran-aligned Houthi movement also fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh. Saudi Arabia's civil defense said on Thursday that the attack on Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, ‌headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, caused material damage to several floors of the tower and nearby buildings, but no injuries were reported, state news agency SPA reported. Earlier in the day, two Western officials briefed by the Saudis said the kingdom is preparing for ​war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year. "Rising Iranian attacks are weighing on Middle Eastern exports just as China ramps up crude imports, reducing oil on water and tightening the oil market," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo. Cumulative losses from the Middle East conflict have now reached 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic meters of gas supply from the Gulf, the International Energy Agency said on Thursday. The ⁠IEA, however, added that the conflict could cut world oil demand by more than 4% by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response. Russia's crude oil output ‌risks falling again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify. Reuters reported on Wednesday that ‌Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, citing industry sources. Separately on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin said that Moscow would hit back hard after Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time this week and said he was dropping any idea of a moratorium on ⁠attacking each other's energy sectors and shipping. Despite the geopolitical risks, signs of ample supply and a meeting between U.S. President Donald ⁠Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Putin, weighed on the market. The three leaders agreed on a symbolic "peace ⁠declaration" at an unprecedented three-way meeting on Thursday and reaffirmed that nuclear war should never be fought and pledged to increase fuel products for all countries. Trump said both he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait ​of Hormuz, and separately said the United States would "see what happens" in its ‌conflict with Iran after January 1, without explaining what the significance of that date might be. Saudi Arabia's crude exports rose nearly 21% in September from August to 5.38 million barrels per day, the highest level since February, data from the Joint Organizations Data Initiative showed on Thursday. Meanwhile, a larger-than-expected build in US crude inventories reported on Wednesday reinforced concerns about a supply overhang, contributing to Brent's 1.3% decline in the previous session and sending WTI down 3.2% to its lowest settlement since August 26. Adding to expectations of surpluses, ​US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Washington was considering ramping up ‌diesel and oil exports to Europe, where the US has become the leading supplier since the US-Iran war began.

title: Oil prices rise as Middle East shipping attacks counter supply surplus outlook - KELO-AM
body: LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) – Oil prices edged up on Thursday following losses in the prior session as worries about Middle East supplies amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed up against expectations for a market surplus. Brent crude futures ​were trading up 24 cents, or 0.26%, at $92.19 a barrel at 0953 GMT. US ‌West Texas Intermediate futures for December were up 5 cents to $83.31. The December contract expires on Friday and the more active January contract was up 12 cents at $82.43. While there was still uncertainty around whether oil prices would have another flare-up or break to the downside, it should be noted that Brent has not been able to ‌stay ​below $90 a barrel, PVM Associates analyst John Evans said. “There is little ⁠chance that any solution to ⁠both the Ukraine war and Iran conflict being achieved by the trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, but in the small chance something comes of it, entering into fresh length in this current environment does not seem altogether attractive,” he said. US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and ​Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, kicked off a three-way meeting, with Trump saying both he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz. Still, risks ⁠remained for Middle East oil supply amid the US-Israeli ⁠war on Iran. Iran’s navy said three oil tankers sailing east of the ​Strait of Hormuz were disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday. On Thursday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement ​fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, but the Saudi Civil Defense ‌agency said the danger had passed. Reuters reported on Wednesday that Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries’ combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, citing industry sources. “Intensifying Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure are keeping supply risks elevated for both crude oil and products, with production ⁠and exports falling,” analysts at ANZ said in a note. A larger-than-expected rise in US oil stockpiles reported on Wednesday, however, weighed on the market outlook. US crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to ⁠417.8 million barrels for the ‌week that ended on November 13, the EIA said, compared with analysts’ ⁠expectations in a Reuters poll for a rise of 58,000 barrels. Brent ​fell 1.3% ‌in the previous session, while WTI dropped 3.2% to its lowest ​point since August ⁠26 on emerging expectations of a supply surplus. Prices have also come under pressure from expectations of higher US interest rates that would cause lower economic growth and slower demand increases for oil. That would also strengthen the dollar, raising prices for non-US buyers paying for dollar-denominated crude in different currencies. (Reporting by Seher Dareen in London, Colleen Howe in Beijing and Siyi Liu in Singapore; Editing by Christian ​Schmollinger and Thomas Derpinghaus)

title: Nvidia stock falls for sixth day as Anthropic debut fails to lift shares - TradingView
body: Nvidia shares NVDA fell 1.5% on Thursday, reversing premarket gains of 1.9% and extending their losing streak to six consecutive trading sessions. The chipmaker failed to benefit from the stock market debut of Anthropic, despite renewed interest in artificial intelligence stocks following the AI company's blockbuster initial public offering. Nvidia stock declined as investors continued to assess concerns surrounding AI infrastructure spending, rising debt and uncertainty following the departure of former chief executive Jensen Huang. Anthropic shares were trading at $98.74, down from their debut price of $111.50 but still around 19% above the IPO price of $83. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.45%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF, which includes Nvidia, declined 1.35%. Anthropic's IPO had initially raised hopes of renewed momentum across the AI sector. The company priced its shares at $83, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, raising approximately $81.3 billion. The listing could indirectly benefit Nvidia by providing Anthropic with additional capital to invest in computing infrastructure. Higher spending on AI training and inference could translate into greater demand for Nvidia's chips. However, that potential benefit did not provide immediate support for the stock on Thursday. Nvidia has been under pressure as investors reassess the sustainability of the AI investment cycle. The stock has fallen 38% since reaching a record closing high of $239.24 on October 6, as concerns about infrastructure spending and financing requirements have weighed on sentiment. The company also faces uncertainty following Huang's resignation last week. Reports concerning allegations involving the former CEO and a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset have added to the negative sentiment surrounding the chipmaker. Nvidia's latest earnings and revenue forecast were strong, but the results were not enough to reverse the stock's decline. Institutional investor filings for the third quarter of 2026 showed that several prominent hedge funds increased or maintained their exposure to Nvidia, although some investors reduced their positions. Tiger Global raised its Nvidia holdings to 12 million shares from 11.2 million, while Altimeter increased its position to 10.01 million shares from 9.41 million. Senator Investment Group also expanded its stake to 444,000 shares from 337,000. Third Point initiated a new position, acquiring 1.5 million shares, while Corvex Management maintained its holding of 16,000 shares. However, Soros Capital reduced its Nvidia position to 10,000 shares from 77,000. Soros Fund also cut its holdings to 859,000 shares from 1.06 million. The mixed positioning suggests that institutional investors had differing views on the chipmaker's prospects during the quarter. Despite the recent decline, Seeking Alpha analyst Lee Bailey upgraded Nvidia to Buy from a previously more cautious stance following the company's third-quarter results. Bailey cited the earnings beat, improved cash conversion and a higher fiscal 2028 growth outlook. The analyst believes the market is undervaluing Nvidia's growth prospects. Bailey set a 12-month price target of $235, implying approximately 50% upside. The upgrade suggests analysts still see value in Nvidia despite recent weakness. However, the stock's performance suggests that strong financial results and positive analyst views have yet to outweigh concerns about the AI investment cycle and uncertainty surrounding the company's leadership. body: On Eastern Time November 19, U.S. stock index futures rose, driven by strong corporate earnings and Anthropic’s high-priced Nasdaq IPO debut under the ticker "ANT," which catalyzed a broad rally in AI-related, storage, and optical stocks. Meanwhile, gold and silver hit 52-week lows, while oil prices stabilized and Bitcoin dipped. Walmart beat revenue estimates and raised guidance, and Fed meeting minutes indicated potential future rate hikes. Intel secured its first external 18A process customer, and Amazon projected robust long-term AI computing demand. TradingKey - On Thursday (Nov. 19) Eastern Time, the three major U.S. stock index futures rose. Anthropic is set to debut on Nasdaq tonight under the ticker "ANT," with its IPO pricing above the preliminary range boosting AI-related stocks. Shares of Alibaba, PDD Holdings, and Palo Alto Networks also gained noticeably in pre-market trading after releasing their earnings reports. As of press time, Nasdaq 100 futures were up 2.18%, S&P 500 futures rose 1.25%, and Dow 30 futures gained 0.65%. In commodities, gold ( XAUUSD ) and silver ( XAGUSD ) hit 52-week lows in tandem. Spot gold briefly fell below $3,700 per ounce, while silver stood at $45.11 per ounce. International oil prices halted their decline and stabilized, with WTI crude futures ( USOIL-F ) at $82.09 per barrel and Brent crude futures ( UKOIL-F ) at $91.73 per barrel. In cryptocurrencies, Bitcoin ( BTCUSD ) briefly fell below $63,000 intraday, with the decline narrowing to 1.18% as of press time. Alibaba ( BABA ) rose over 4% premarket as cloud business growth accelerated. Alibaba reported revenue of 271.519 billion yuan for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 10% year-over-year, while adjusted EBITA reached 32.636 billion yuan, up 260% year-over-year. Revenue from AI cloud and computing services grew 53% year-over-year, with external customer revenue up 64% and adjusted EBITA for the related business jumping 121% year-over-year. Accelerated cloud growth and improving profitability have become the central focus for the market. PDD Holdings ( PDD ) surged nearly 10% premarket following its earnings release. PDD Holdings rose nearly 10% in premarket trading after reporting third-quarter revenue of approximately 108.3 billion yuan, roughly flat year-over-year. The market is closely watching how its ongoing investments in merchant support and supply chain initiatives will affect future growth and profitability. Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) jumped over 9% premarket after raising its full-year revenue guidance and announcing plans to acquire Applied Compute. The company reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $3.445 billion, up 39% year-over-year, with next-generation security annual recurring revenue reaching $9.73 billion, up 66% year-over-year. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to between $14.52 billion and $14.57 billion and announced its plan to acquire AI firm Applied Compute to expand its enterprise AI security business. Investors in Anthropic rose broadly premarket, with Google and Micron Technology up more than 3%. Google parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ) and Micron Technology ( MU ) rose over 3%, while AMD ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), and Zoom ( ZM ) gained more than 2%; Amazon ( AMZN ) rose nearly 2%, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) were up over 1%. The market is assessing the impact of Anthropic's listing on the value of its investors' holdings and AI business prospects. Storage and memory stocks advanced across the board premarket, with SK Hynix gaining more than 6%. SK Hynix ( SKHY ) rose over 6%, SanDisk ( SNDK ), Micron Technology, and Silicon Motion ( SIMO ) climbed over 4%, and Seagate Technology ( STX ) and Western Digital ( WDC ) gained more than 3%. The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights NVIDIA, Cisco Systems and AMD - Yahoo Finance
body: Chicago, IL – November 19, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: NVIDIA Corporation NVDA, Cisco Systems, Inc CSCO and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD. Despite NVIDIA Corporation 's strong quarterly performance, leadership uncertainty and rising artificial intelligence (AI) spending concerns could pose a challenge in the future. However, Cisco Systems, Inc. 's stable management and diversified business portfolio could position it as a better stock to buy now. Let's explore – NVIDIA delivered another strong quarter, with revenues surging 103% year over year to $115.8 billion in the fiscal third quarter of 2027, according to the company's Nov. 17 press release. It also posted a 20% sequential rise from $96.2 billion in the previous quarter. NVIDIA's triple-digit growth rate highlighted that strong AI spending benefited the company, with tech companies investing significantly in computing capacity. The Data Center business remains its primary growth driver, with revenues jumping 110% year over year and 21% sequentially to $107.6 billion. This result shows NVIDIA is making the most of hyperscalers' massive investments in AI-driven data centers. By the way, NVIDIA is converting its impressive revenue growth into noteworthy profits as well. Its GAAP net income jumped 105% year over year to $65.3 billion. Looking ahead, NVIDIA expects revenues of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2027, which would represent a 12% sequential rise. That's a strong revenue growth projection, especially since it doesn't include China-related Data Center compute revenues. NVIDIA also expects its earnings outlook to remain strong in the fiscal fourth quarter. NVIDIA's strong fiscal third-quarter performance and optimistic fiscal fourth-quarter outlook suggest the company is not only benefiting from the AI boom but also converting that growth into solid revenues and earnings growth. However, the latest controversy surrounding NVIDIA's boardroom drama and the subsequent ouster of Jensen Huang as CEO is a significant concern for investors in the future. NVIDIA will lose a visionary leader, whose continuous innovation helped the company maintain a competitive position in the rapidly evolving AI market. His earlier investments in graphics processing units helped NVIDIA establish a competitive advantage against its peers. He also played a crucial role in building partnerships among major tech players, and his departure could give an undue advantage to rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. . Moving ahead, NVIDIA's capability to sustain an extraordinary growth rate without Huang at the helm will be closely monitored, and any leadership uncertainty could dent investors' confidence. But as NVIDIA grapples with leadership succession, Cisco stands out for its stable succession planning and management continuity. The company's CEO, Chuck Robbins, has held the position since 2015 and has assured investors that in his absence, the company's strategic decisions and execution won't be hampered. Growing concerns about the sustainability of AI spending could create additional uncertainty around NVIDIA's future growth trajectory. Cisco, on the other hand, has a diversified revenue stream, making it less dependent on the AI boom. It can benefit from broader IT spending, providing additional growth opportunities, and could offer greater resilience if AI-related spending moderates. Cisco reported record revenues of $18.5 billion in the fiscal first quarter of 2027, up 24% year over year, according to the company's Nov. 12 press release. However, Cisco's revenue growth wasn't only dependent on AI investments by hyperscalers; it was broad-based, across various business segments like networking, cybersecurity, collaboration and software.
